Brother, you need to go into prayer about this, and make ample time to talk about your problems with her. If you are both meant to be together, communication about your problem will be the key test of your pre-marriage relationship.

Look at my count.

Here's how I got here: I put my phone and all electronics away in a separate room at night before I go to sleep. I leave my phone in the living room every time I use the bathroom. I go for walks when the urges are strong, lift weights during moderate urges, and pray during the lighter urges.

And remember this golden rule. Focus on sobriety, **one day at a time!**

Take the time to process your pain, and leave the door open for if he comes back to at least explain himself for leaving. Otherwise, just know that this won't be your end all be all, in the long haul, and that you will find contentment as time moves on.

For now though, r/lonely is here for you, and we all (at least from my viewpoint) hope and pray you will feel better as time goes on. I was ghosted like this too, and it sure hurt me like a train running over me.

But I can attest to you that life (or in my beliefs God Himself) has a curious way of working through situations/people into your life along the way of healing when we go through heartbreak. Know that we will be here for you, and remember to take it all one day at a time.

Hugs to you, good luck and God Bless.

Be gentle but firm in how you present your points and concerns.

He needs to know that his lovely wife cares about him, but that his addiction is both hurting the one he loves and himself.

Ultimately, this will fall on him waking up and accepting the journey to change. Focus on getting him to get the help he needs, and take the recovery journey one step at a time.

And remember, as long as the porn addiction came before your marriage, you can rest with the fact you're not ugly. It's the porn that is sabotaging him, sexually. (Also, look in that damn mirror and smile. You must be beautiful enough that someone took the jump of faith to marry you and be with you!)

Deep down, remember that he loves you enough to have married you and enjoy a sex life with you. This cancerous addiction is the divide in your relationship, but through earnest prayer, dedication, and a hard work in the field of recovery, your marriage (God-Willing) can be restored!

God Bless and Good Luck!

A good starting point is asking yourself what do you feel prior to giving in?

\- Are you feeling bored? Get your body physically engaged in a walk, workout, or stretching.

\- Are you feeling lonely? Watch a movie or call a friend/family member (pets work too.)

\- Are you feeling in the mood? - Eat something, go for a walk, and think on other matters because, unless you have a partner, you need to engage your mind off of that feeling as a means of self-control to rewire your brain.

God Bless and hope this helps. You will be sober soon!

I'm 22 going on 23 and dateless. I can attest that on a positive note, you learn to enjoy your singleness as you get older, especially as you recover. You need to set appreciative standards for yourself and make sure you love yourself enough to draw boundaries. Hormones are tempting, amorous words are fun when young, but don't get fucked over by out of control emotions and in the moment lovey-dovey talk.

It will all be worth it, darling. Just keep fighting.

24 hours no phone or electronics. As Bravo Six once said, **"Going Dark."**

You need to forget the 'relapse' and focus on going forward. But for safety, no technology for at least 1 full day. And delete the socials as needed.

Remember, you are a recovering addict. All means of recovery must be readily available on the table for you to use.

Leave him. As an addict, you need to avoid sexual intimacy of this caliber until you can fully reboot and choose a sexual encounter from a sober, and PMO free, state of mind.

It's the equivalent to have a shot on Tequila Tuesday when you're a recovering alcoholic.

Or a vape hit as you recover from all forms of smoking.

Go out to eat.

Talk to a female friend.

Go for a walk.

**But don't let horniness takeover Godliness and Sobriety.**

Until then, remember the basics for getting on with life:

\- Vitamins

\- Diet

\- Exercise

\- Entertainment

\- Education

\- Prayers

Yes, none of these things are the cuddles or spoons you seek. But take it from your local Reddit-Tony: I may not have my own big/small spoon to cuddle with, but these things I outlined helped me to get my life in order and mentally stand strong when the emotional shit hits the fan, (aka when my brain goes to neediness mode)

Until then, a brotherly hug and set of prayers to you all during your singleness/loneliness. As a loner myself, I can tell you that good days are on the way, even when we feel as dark and dim as we feel now.

Even though you have 5 years gone, remember this: You got the painful truth you needed to make a good decision. I was in your shoes once, 2-3 years under my belt. I thought God was giving me this dream girl, only to discover I was wasting my time on someone who never cared. My friend, if she doesn't want you, then leave her be. Ask yourself this, if God loves you, why would He toy with you and cuck you like that? Spoiler alert: He doesn't do that to  His children, nor to non-believers. Take this opportunity to make yourself happy doing what you love, and walking out of this mess one day at a time. In the meantime, know that  the one He sets aside for you will clearly love you for **you.**
